selected.rationale: Redis is the sole basket state store; a network loss makes Basket.API unable to read/write carts, exposing missing fallback and causing full checkout availability loss.

Basket.API publishes the checkout integration event directly to RabbitMQ; losing this message silently prevents order creation, confirming the lack of durable outbox or reliable retry on this critical path.

Placing an order is a critical user action; injecting delay on webapp->ordering-api tests whether the HTTP client has a bounded timeout, exposing unbounded latency propagation and possible resource exhaustion.
Cart retrieval/update is on the main shopping path; a loss without retry produces immediate 5xx and blocks checkout, demonstrating missing resilience in the webapp-to-basket call.
Identity is needed for login and authorization; losing this synchronous edge makes the storefront unavailable to users and verifies there is no degraded-mode path or retry protection.
Catalog integration events drive downstream product data; loss on this RabbitMQ edge can permanently desynchronize services that consume catalog changes, exposing missing recovery/retry.
The mobile BFF exposes ordering to clients; an injected delay will reveal whether the BFF applies any timeout/circuit breaker, turning Ordering.API slowness into unbounded mobile user wait.
Catalog data is fetched for storefront browsing; a delay on webapp->catalog-api stresses the lack of caching/timeout and can make the whole web UI unresponsive.
